newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish big western cities lead investment ranking.
newsitem.headline: Polish big western cities lead investment ranking.

text.p: Large western Polish cities are the country's most attractive locations for investment, showed a ranking by the independent Gdansk Market Economy Institute (IBnGR) published on Wednesday.

Wojciech Dziemianowicz, who co-authored the ranking, told a news conference that cities with a population of more than 250,000 and close to the western border won the highest marks in the ranking. He said the institute evaluated the cities taking into account such factors as the depth of the local market, the quality of labour, social climate and the quality of infrastructure and transport links.

"A city attractiveness depends largely on its size, the most attractive (for investments) are those with more than 250,000 people...the closer to the western border, the more attractive the city is," he said.

Dziemianowicz said seven cities made into the top 'A' category: the centrally located capital Warsaw, southern historic city of Krakow, port city of Gdansk and western cities of Katowice, Poznan, Szczecin and Wroclaw.
He said IBnGR planned to prepare such rankings on an annual basis. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
